verdicts.reason: The line is now WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` — a template literal with no interpolation left, a genuine nit. The 'most lint configs flag it' rationale does not hold for this repo: packages/config/eslint-preset.js enables no quotes/no-useless-template-literal rule and @typescript-eslint 'recommended' does not include one.

The diff adds apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts plus two _utils/oauth helpers and rewires nine refresh paths without a single test file; the google-persists-wrapper and zoho-bigin userId defects are both trivially unit-testable.

appStoreMetadata is keyed by dirName (googlecalendar, office365calendar, office365video, zoomvideo, larkcalendar) while App.slug in prisma/schema.prisma holds the slug (google-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, zoom, lark-calendar), so appStoreMetadata[app.slug] is undefined and the handler 404s for exactly the apps this PR wires up.
After persisting accessTokenParsed.data, the returned jsforce.Connection is still built from credentialKey.instance_url / credentialKey.access_token, the values read before the refresh.

`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` yields string | undefined, not boolean; the exported constant is only used in truthiness checks today, but the name and type invite misuse.

Node lowercases incoming header keys, so a mixed-case CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME makes the lookup undefined and every request 403s with 'Invalid webhook secret'; the only warning is the one-line .env.example comment, as the claim states.

The new outbound fetch to the sync endpoint has no try/catch; a network failure rejects and propagates. 'Unhandled' overstates it (google/hubspot/zohocrm/lark wrap their calls), but the gap is real for a newly introduced dependency.
The file calls prisma.credential.update but has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`; the bare identifier only type-checks because packages/prisma/index.ts has `declare global { var prisma }`.

When the parsed data has no refresh_token the code writes the literal string "refresh_token"; on the sync path minimumTokenResponseSchema strips everything but access_token, so this always fires and office365 then merges it over the real refresh token (CalendarService.ts:264) before persisting.

refreshOAuthTokens only uses the sync endpoint when userId is truthy, but parseRefreshTokenResponse switches schema on the env vars alone, so team credentials (userId null) get a genuine provider response parsed by minimumTokenResponseSchema, which strips every field except access_token.

`const credentialId = credential.id` is passed as refreshOAuthTokens' third argument (userId), which is POSTed as calcomUserId; the line number cited is off by a few but the call site and the defect are exactly as described.

findFirst-then-create with no unique constraint on (userId, appId) — the Credential model only has @@index([userId]) and @@index([appId]) — so two concurrent webhook calls can both miss and both insert.
Same defect: the DB is updated with the fresh token but the Connection handed back to the caller carries credentialKey.access_token from before the refresh.

The line is genuinely broken and must be fixed, but not for the stated reason: `z.string().toString()` is legal JS and evaluates to "[object Object]", so both computed keys collide on one meaningless property and the schema silently degrades to `{ access_token: string }` — there is no runtime error and Zod accepts it.
parseRefreshTokenResponse throws when success is false, so `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` can only ever take the truthy branch — leftover from the old safeParse call.
An empty `/** */` sits directly above the only new public entry point; compare the documented handler in apps/web/pages/api/sync/helpscout/index.ts.
No req.method guard anywhere in the handler, while the repo's comparable webhook and app-store add/callback handlers open with `if (req.method !== "POST"/"GET") return res.status(405)`.
The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT passes no AbortSignal/timeout, and this call sits inside the booking/availability path.

Salesforce imports only parseRefreshTokenResponse and calls login.salesforce.com directly; every other adapter touched by this PR routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so salesforce silently opts out of credential sync.
`.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError out of an unwrapped Next.js API handler, which Next turns into a 500; the repo convention (helpscout webhook) is safeParse then `res.status(400)`.

The outbound POST carries only calcomUserId and appSlug — no shared secret, no header — while the inbound webhook enforces CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET; the asymmetry is verifiable in the code even if the intent (internal-network endpoint) is not.

The diff deletes the console.error that dumped tokenResponse.error and the raw MS response; the replacement path throws a bare `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` from parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:22 with no context.
Inverted: this was the pre-change behaviour. parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on parse failure, so prisma.credential.update on line 265 is never reached — nothing stale is persisted.
Same defect, stated most precisely: the Connection uses credentialKey.access_token / credentialKey.instance_url rather than accessTokenParsed.data.

Node does not array-ify arbitrary duplicate headers (only set-cookie); duplicates of a custom header are joined with ", ". And even if an array arrived, `array !== string` is true, which 403s the request — the opposite of the claimed auth bypass.

symmetricDecrypt calls crypto.createDecipheriv and decipher.final, both of which throw synchronously on a bad key length or bad ciphertext, and the result is fed straight to JSON.parse — neither is wrapped, so tampered input yields a 500.

`this.conn = this.getClient(credential).then((c) => c)` attaches no rejection handler, and this PR makes getClient reject far more often (network fetch, HttpError on statusText, Promise.reject on parse failure) before any consumer awaits this.conn.

On the sync path refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError (swallowed by the surrounding catch, leaving the refresh a silent no-op).
Same defect: credential.id is handed to the userId parameter and sent as calcomUserId.

Both call sites are as described — google reads res?.data, hubspot annotates the result `HubspotToken` and immediately reads hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn — while refreshOAuthTokens returns a Response on the sync path.
`refreshFunction: () => any` erases the return type at every one of the nine call sites, which is precisely why the Response-vs-token-object mismatch compiles.

Confirmed both halves: `declare global { var prisma }` makes the bare identifier type-check, and `globalThis.prisma = prisma` is guarded by `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production")`, so in production the reference is undefined and getClient throws a TypeError.

The Response is returned without checking response.ok or inspecting the body, so a 4xx/5xx or an HTML error page from the self-hoster's endpoint is passed on to callers as if it were a token response.
Same defect stated from the helper's side: the third parameter is userId and is serialised as calcomUserId.
Correct: no method guard, and for a GET req.body is undefined so the zod .parse on line 31 throws and Next returns 500.

The JSON.parse result is untyped and written straight into credential.key on both the update and create branches with no per-app key-schema validation, so a bad payload only surfaces later when an adapter parses the credential.
Same issue; the cited convention exists — the helpscout webhook returns `405 Method not allowed` for anything but POST.
Both halves check out: the schema parse (and the later JSON.parse) throw into Next's default 500 handler, and there is no method guard.
Same as c026 — createDecipheriv/final and JSON.parse are all unguarded, so malformed keys produce a 500.

getClient reads credential.key, refreshes, and writes the new key with no transaction or version check; because it runs on every construction (see c044) concurrent requests for the same credential do interleave read-modify-write.

The count is right: google, hubspot, lark, office365calendar, office365video, webex, zohocrm and zoomvideo all pass credential.userId; only zoho-bigin passes credential.id, so an integer that is a valid other user's id can be sent as calcomUserId.
Accurate on all three points: .parse instead of the repo's safeParse-then-400 pattern, and neither symmetricDecrypt nor JSON.parse is wrapped.
Confirmed: with both env vars set the constant's value is the literal CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY string, exported under an _ENABLED name from a widely imported module.

The constructor calls getClient unconditionally and getClient always POSTs to the token endpoint and writes the credential row — there is no isExpired/isTokenValid guard like office365calendar:236, zoho-bigin:55 or zoomvideo.

Using the reason phrase as the success test is wrong — response.ok is the correct check, and the thrown HttpError message is whatever statusText happens to be. The HTTP/2 rationale is shaky though: Node's fetch (undici) speaks HTTP/1.1 and does populate statusText, so the 'successful 200 becomes a 400' failure does not occur today.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result and google assigns it straight to `key` in prisma.credential.update, so credential.key becomes { success: true, data: {...} } and every later googleCredentialSchema.parse of that credential fails.
CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET sits after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY; the three sibling additions were placed alphabetically, so this one is the odd entry out.
req.headers keys are lowercased by Node, so an env var set in mixed case makes the lookup undefined and the secret check always fails; no .toLowerCase() is applied to the configured name.
Same defect: accessToken comes from credentialKey, read at line 72 before the refresh, so the current request still uses the old token.

Confirmed: the redirectUri now hardcodes "zoho-bigin" while appConfig is still imported and used two lines above (getAppKeysFromSlug(appConfig.slug)) and below (appConfig.scope); the change is unrelated to credential sync.
